items.title: At least 37 dead and hundreds evacuated after strike on Kyiv weapons depot
items.description: An investigation has begun into the storage of weapons for Ukraine's military near a residential area.

items.title: Niger's junta says 'regaining control' after clashes in capital
items.description: Niger's ​defense ​ministry said the armed forces were ​progressively ‌retaking ⁠control ‌of sites targeted in ⁠an overnight attack on ​the ‌capital Niamey, according to a ‌statement read ​on state television, which resumed broadcasting ​on ​Saturday after ​temporarily going ​offline.

items.title: Kremlin Says Peace Talks on ‘Deep Pause’
items.description: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov announced on Friday that peace negotiations with Ukraine are on a “deep pause” as Russian forces press their offensive in the east. items.title: Srebrenica survivor Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death
items.description: Ahmed Hrustanovic reflects on Ratko Mladic's death with NPR's Scott Simon. All of Hrustanovic's adult male relatives died in the Srebrenica Massacre engineered by Mladic.

items.title: Dozens dead after Russian strike on depot near Kyiv
items.description: The depot appeared to have been storing explosives. The blast reportedly damaged residential areas, as well as a care home for the elderly and disabled people.

items.title: Iran’s leaders acknowledge economic toll of war, pledge diplomacy, defence
items.description: Iran's president said sanctions and the US naval blockade had caused exports and imports to slump by nearly 35 percent.

items.title: Four children killed as separate attacks in Gaza destroy aid supplies
items.description: Israeli attacks killed four children and destroyed humanitarian aid supplies in what turned out to be a deadly week in war-ravaged Gaza, the UN emergency relief agency, OCHA, said on Friday.

items.title: Kremlin Says Ukraine Peace Talks on ‘Deep Pause’
items.description: The New York Times reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow this week to push the Kremlin towards a peace deal.

items.title: The man behind Srebrenica: Ratko Mladic dies at 84
items.description: For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian War. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and of other war crimes. Now he has died in detention at The Hague.

items.title: In Sudan’s civil war, both sides target journalists
items.description: Local journalists reporting on Sudan’s civil war and humanitarian crisis there are facing a campaign of intimidation by rival military forces.
